subject: Post-call: FinTechAI pricing & latency trade-offs / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma@fintechai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (pricing / latency trade-offs)

Thanks for the time earlier, Emma — good call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on pricing and latency trade-offs.

Summary of what you shared
- Workload: conversational assistant for banking support (NLP + retrieval augmentation)
- Monthly token estimate: ~100M tokens/month (current pilot), with potential to grow to 500M over 12 months.
- Typical prompt + response length: ~150 tokens average (50 prompt + 100 response).
- Peak concurrency: ~12 QPS during business hours; sustained baseline ~2-3 QPS.
- Latency SLO: P95 target ~200-300ms for interactive flows; some background tasks can be relaxed.
- Budget guidance: outlined target of $20–$35 per 1M tokens (top of funnel asks $/1M token target).

Key trade-offs we discussed
- Hosted API (standard): fastest time to value, supports streaming. Unit price higher but no infra commitment; good for initial pilot.
- Dedicated / reserved capacity: lower effective unit cost at commit, predictable throughput, better P95 latency under load (less noisy neighbors), recommended if you need steady throughput and tight SLOs.
- Batching & KV cache: can reduce per-token cost ~15–35% depending on request patterns; increases tail latency unless we configure SLO-driven batching.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming improves perceived latency for users but may increase token/time-based cost; it also affects how we provision concurrency.

Proposed next steps
1) You share the sample usage CSV (thanks — attached) so we can run a rough unit-economics model.
2) We’ll produce 2 pricing options: Hosted estimate (no commit) and Dedicated reserved capacity estimate (3–12 month commit tiers) with effective $/1M token targets and expected P95 latency.
3) If pricing and SLAs look good, pilot a small dedicated pool for 1 month (can be time-boxed / canary traffic) to validate P95 latency and cost.

Action items
- Emma: confirm the 100M/month baseline and attach a week of sample traffic (request/response lengths + timestamps).
- FinTechAI procurement: share any procurement timeline or PO process.
- Redwood: share pricing PDF and a first-pass estimate by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: FinTechAI_usage_sample.csv (please confirm sample is representative)

Thanks — I’ll get the initial estimate together and loop in engineering for latency guidance.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (pricing / latency trade-offs)

Emma — thanks for the sample, that helps a lot. Below is a first-pass, high-level estimate and suggested config. This is intentionally conservative; we’ll run a more precise model after ingesting the CSV.

Quick numbers (ballpark) based on the 120M/month baseline and average 150 tokens/session:
Option A — Hosted API (no commit)- Unit price (approx): $60 / 1M tokens (streaming enabled)- Expected latency: median ~80–120ms; P95 ~300–450ms under bursty load- Pros: fastest to deploy, supports streaming out-of-the-box; no commit.

Option B — Dedicated Reserved Capacity (recommended if you need stable P95 & lower unit cost)- Commit tiers: 3-month / 12-month options. Effective unit cost (example): $18–$28 / 1M tokens depending on commit size and throughput patterns. For your 120M baseline, 12-month commit estimate ~ $22 / 1M tokens effective; at 300–400M scale we get to ~$18 / 1M.- Expected latency: P95 ~120–220ms with appropriate instance sizing and KV caching; streaming supported but we recommend small batching window + micro-batching to smooth tail latency.- Pros: predictable costs, better P95 and isolation.

Batching & caching guidance
- Aggressive batching (large windows) reduces unit cost but adds tail latency — not ideal for interactive flows.
- SLO-driven batching: we can set max batching delay (e.g., 10–25ms) to capture most batching benefits while keeping P95 constraints. Expected token-cost reduction: ~15–30% depending on request shape.
- KV caching reduces repeated prompt tokens (useful for similar contexts) — may cut token usage for repeated prompts by 10–25%.

Streaming trade-offs
- Streaming is great for perceived latency; however streaming can increase connection time and complicate batching. For interactive UX we recommend streaming + small max-batch delay. For background jobs use non-streaming and larger batches.

Recommended pilot config
- 5% canary: provision a small dedicated pool (1–2 GPUs depending on model choice) for two weeks; enable streaming + max-batch-delay=15ms and KV cache.- Success criteria: P95 <= 250ms for interactive flows, total effective cost <= $30 / 1M tokens for pilot traffic.

Next steps
- We’ll produce a formal PDF with Hosted vs Dedicated pricing by EOD tomorrow (attaching draft).- If you’re OK, we’ll set up a 30-min runbook review with engineering to validate instance sizing and SLO-driven batching settings.

Attaching: redwood_pricing_tiers_v2.pdf (draft).

Best,
Marissa

Quick internal note — copying the thread for context. My read: FinTechAI is a good fit for a time-boxed dedicated pilot. Recommended internal plan: 
- Engineering: prepare runbook for 1–2 GPU pool, include SLO-driven batching knobs (max-batch-delay param) and KV caching.
- Pricing: offer a 6-week trial at an effective $25/1M tokens for the pilot (apply as a credit against a later 12-mo commit). This keeps them within target while we validate latency.
- CS/Support: assign one eng on-call during the canary window.

Next internal steps: Rachel to own runbook + sizing; Marissa to confirm pilot window and procurement contacts.
